isotomics.basicDeltaOperations¶

isotomics.basicDeltaOperations.compareRelDelta(atomID, deltaStd, deltaSmp)¶

Compute sample-relative-to-standard delta in CRF space.

This comparison accounts for non-additivity of delta values.

Parameters:

  • atomID – Isotope key passed to deltaToConcentration().

  • deltaStd – Delta value of the standard (denominator).

  • deltaSmp – Delta value of the sample (numerator).

Returns:

Sample-relative-to-standard delta value.

Return type:

float

Example

>>> compareRelDelta("13C", -10, -20)
-10.101010101010166
isotomics.basicDeltaOperations.concentrationToM1Ratio(concentrationTuple)¶

Compute the M+1-to-unsubstituted ratio from a concentration vector.

Parameters:

concentrationTuple – Four-element concentration vector in the internal isotope ordering.

Returns:

Ratio of the mass-1 isotope to the unsubstituted isotope.

Return type:

float

Example

>>> concentrationToM1Ratio((0.989052963984032, 0.010947036015968062, 0, 0))
0.0110682
isotomics.basicDeltaOperations.deltaToConcentration(atomIdentity, delta)¶

Convert a delta value into internal isotope concentrations.

For isotope systems with multiple rare isotopes (for example O and S), additional isotope concentrations are set using the mass-scaling rules used by Isotomics.

Parameters:

  • atomIdentity – Isotope key identifying the ratio system (for example, "13C", "15N", "D", "17O", "33S").

  • delta – Delta value in per mil for the specified isotope system.

Returns:

Concentrations in internal isotope ordering: (unsubstituted, M+1, M+2, M+3). For systems with fewer than four components, unused entries are 0.

Return type:

tuple[float, float, float, float]

Example

>>> deltaToConcentration("13C", -10)
(0.989052963984032, 0.010947036015968062, 0, 0)
isotomics.basicDeltaOperations.ratioToDelta(atomIdentity, ratio)¶

Convert an isotope ratio into a delta value.

Parameters:

  • atomIdentity – Isotope key of interest.

  • ratio – Isotope ratio relative to the unsubstituted isotope.

Returns:

Delta value for the provided isotope ratio.

Return type:

float

Example

>>> ratioToDelta("13C", 0.0110682)
-10.000000000000009
isotomics.basicDeltaOperations.twoDeltasToConcentration(atomIdentity, deltaTuple)¶

Convert paired delta constraints into isotope concentrations.

This variant handles systems where two deltas are explicitly constrained (17/18O or 33/34S), instead of deriving the second via mass scaling.

Parameters:

  • atomIdentity – "O" or "S".

  • deltaTuple – Two-element tuple. First value is 17O or 33S delta; second value is 18O or 34S delta.

Returns:

Concentration vector for the isotope system. For sulfur, ordering is (32S, 33S, 34S, 36S).

Return type:

tuple[float, float, float, float]

Example

>>> twoDeltasToConcentration("O", (-10, -20))
(0.9976642714007893, 0.00037522253013810825, 0.001960506069072605, 0)
